topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening introduces the lecturer and outlines the scope, themes, and learning outcomes for understanding what causes cancer.

topics.label: Frameworks of Cancer Causation: Genetics, Chance, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental causes of cancer development by exploring the interplay between endogenous mutations, inherited risks, environmental exposures, and geographic epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Carcinogenic Agents, Metabolic Activation, and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific biological, physical, and chemical agents to explain the molecular mechanisms of direct DNA damage, xenobiotic metabolic activation, and inflammatory tumor promotion.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to identify carcinogens and evaluate cancer risk.
